name: Amangani
positioning: Mountain resort on East Gros Ventre Butte overlooking Jackson, Wyoming, with redwood and sandstone interiors designed by Ed Tuttle
best_for: Travelers who want a Teton-view base for wildlife tours, hiking and winter snowshoeing
Skiers who are happy with a winter shuttle to Jackson Hole Mountain Resort rather than slopeside access

facts.text: Amangani is high atop East Gros Ventre Butte, overlooking Jackson, Wyoming.
The building was designed by architect Ed Tuttle and is long and slender, with two elongated wings on either side of a central hub.
All suites have gas fireplaces, king-sized beds, deep soaker tubs and plush sitting areas.
The Grill menu features dishes inspired by the Rocky Mountains, such as caribou sausage and elk T-bone steaks.
Private dining experiences featuring a five-course tasting menu are available.
Chefs can pack a gourmet picnic for breakfast or lunch for guests heading out on an adventure.
The heated outdoor pool and hot tub have mountain views.
Guests can book private yoga classes, guided meditation sessions and crystal sound baths.
In winter the hotel offers shuttle transportation to the Jackson Hole Mountain Resort.
In winter season guests have access to the Amangani Ski Lounge at the base of the Jackson Hole Mountain Resort.
Guests have access to hiking routes and snowshoe trails, with complimentary snowshoes during the winter.

highlights.text: Pacific redwood panels cover the walls and ceilings, offset by floor-to-ceiling columns of Oklahoma sandstone.
Every room has southwest-facing, floor-to-ceiling windows framing the Snake River Valley below and the Tetons above.
The signature wildlife tour is led by a private guide to wildlife-spotting sites in the National Elk Refuge, Grand Teton National Park and surrounding areas.
The spa has Amangani-specific treatments, including a ritual with a peppermint foot scrub and a customized massage with warm basalt stones and amethyst crystals.
The Grand Teton Suite is a rare corner suite at the far northwest end of the building, with a wall of windows facing Grand Teton.

considerations.text: Amangani is not a slopeside hotel, so ski-in, ski-out access is not available.
The hotel has no kids' club, and its decor feels distinctly adult.
WhataHotel notes the remote mountain location requires planning for dining and activities.
